Random Forest Imputation

impute.rfsrc.Rd

Imputes missing values using random forests. The default is on-the-fly imputation (OTFI), with supervised or unsupervised splitting, including an optional autoencoder. Alternatively, missForest predicts missing values one variable or group of variables at a time. Returns an imputed data frame.

# S3 method for class 'rfsrc'
impute(formula, data,
  ntree = 100, nodesize = 1, nsplit = 10,
  nimpute = 2, fast = FALSE, blocks,
  mf.q, max.iter = 10, eps = 0.01,
  ytry = NULL, always.use = NULL, verbose = TRUE,
  full.sweep = FALSE, restore.integer = TRUE,
  ...)

Arguments

formula

Model formula specifying the responses and predictors for OTFI. Omit it for unsupervised splitting, when no outcome is designated. Ignored for missForest.

data

Data to be imputed. Matrices, tibbles, and data.table objects are converted to a plain data frame. Column names must be unique and nonempty, each column must be a vector, and numeric values must be finite or missing. Bare vectors and nested matrix or list columns are not supported.

ntree

Number of trees grown for each imputation forest.

nodesize

Minimum terminal node size in each tree.

nsplit

Non-negative integer for specifying random splitting.

nimpute

Number of OTFI iterations. Ignored for missForest, whose iterations are controlled by max.iter and eps.

fast

If TRUE, uses fast forest settings to reduce computation. May reduce imputation accuracy.

blocks

Number of row blocks for the main imputation fits. May improve speed for large data, but can reduce imputation accuracy. If omitted, fits use all rows. See Details.

mf.q

Selects missForest when supplied. With mf.q = 1 and always.use = NULL, variables are imputed one at a time. Other positive values select multivariate missForest and specify an approximate fraction (below 1) or number (above 1) of variables with missing values to include in each response group. Takes precedence over splitrule = "auto". See Details.

max.iter

Maximum number of missForest iterations. Must be a positive integer.

eps

Minimum decrease in the change between successive missForest imputations required to continue iterating. Must be finite and nonnegative. See Details.

ytry

Number of response variables used for unsupervised OTFI. With the default splitting method, pseudo-responses are selected for each candidate splitting variable; the default is min(p - 1, max(25, ceiling(sqrt(p)))). With splitrule = "auto", response copies are selected at each node; the default is p, and a smaller positive integer can be supplied. Here p is the number of variables remaining after all-missing columns are removed. Used when formula and mf.q are omitted.

always.use

Names of variables to include in every response group for multivariate missForest. With mf.q supplied, any non-NULL value selects the multivariate version, even if mf.q = 1. Empty vectors and names not present in the data add no responses but still select this version. Ignored for OTFI.

verbose

If TRUE, prints progress during missForest imputation and the optional final sweep.

full.sweep

If TRUE, performs one additional pass after either imputation method. Each variable with missing values in the original data is predicted from the current imputed values of the other variables. Only originally missing entries are replaced. See Details.

restore.integer

If TRUE, rounds imputed values to integers for columns stored as R integers or whose observed numeric values are all integer-valued. Observed values are preserved. Numeric columns retain numeric storage. Original integer columns are returned as integer vectors only when all nonmissing completed values are integral and within R's integer range; otherwise they retain numeric storage. Set to FALSE to keep unrounded imputations. See Details for the integer-detection tolerance.

...

Additional forest controls for the main imputation: mtry, splitrule, bootstrap, sampsize, and samptype. Use splitrule = "auto" for autoencoder splitting when formula and mf.q are omitted. Supplying mf.q selects missForest and ignores the "auto" setting. Controls for the optional final sweep are supplied separately in the named list full.sweep.options. This list accepts the same controls, plus ntree (default 500), nodesize (default NULL), and nsplit (default 10).

Details

Two approaches are available. The default, on-the-fly imputation (OTFI), handles missing values during tree construction and obtains final imputations from terminal nodes. Supplying mf.q selects missForest, which repeatedly uses the other variables to impute each variable or group of variables with missing values. Both approaches support numeric and categorical data. The function returns the imputed data frame; fitted forests and performance summaries are not returned.

On-the-fly imputation (OTFI)

OTFI is the approach underlying na.action = "na.impute" in rfsrc and predict.rfsrc. Tang and Ishwaran (2017, Sections 2.3–2.4) describe the method for both the supervised and unsupervised case.

Split statistics are calculated from the observed values of the variables involved. If an observation is missing the value of the chosen splitting variable, a value is drawn from that variable's observed inbag values in the node to determine its daughter node. This draw is temporary: it is discarded after assignment, and the entry is treated as missing again at the next node. Final replacements are obtained separately from observed values in the terminal nodes and combined across trees.

With a response formula, OTFI uses supervised splitting guided by the specified outcome. For example, Ozone ~ . uses Ozone to guide the splits while imputing missing responses and predictors.

With no formula, OTFI uses unsupervised splitting to learn relationships among the variables. At each node, each of mtry candidate splitting variables is evaluated against ytry randomly selected pseudo-responses using a multivariate composite splitting rule. The best split is selected.

Additionally, for unsupervised data, setting splitrule = "auto" implements a autoencoder type method which regresses variables against themselves. Temporary copies serve as multivariate responses, and the original variables serve as predictors. Missing entries remain missing in both copies for OTFI to process. All response variables are used by default (ytry = p). The temporary responses are discarded after imputation; only the completed original variables are returned or used in the optional final sweep. Other splitrule settings are ignored when the formula is omitted.

nimpute controls the number of OTFI iterations. With a formula, splitrule = "random" can be used for completely random splitting.

missForest

missForest is an unsupervised imputation procedure in the sense that no outcome needs to be designated: every variable can be imputed using the others. Its individual forests use supervised regression or classification. The formula argument is ignored; an outcome column included in data is treated like any other variable.

The implementation first fills missing values using a small forest with completely random splitting. These initial imputations supply values for the predictors in subsequent fits.

With mf.q = 1 and always.use = NULL, the method follows the variable-by-variable approach of Stekhoven and Buehlmann (2012). For each variable with missing values, a forest is fit using the rows where that variable was observed. Its missing entries are replaced by predictions from this forest. Later fits use the imputations already updated for earlier variables, and the process repeats.

The multivariate extension groups variables with missing values and imputes each group using the remaining variables (Tang and Ishwaran, 2017, Section 2.5). Group sizes are approximate and controlled by mf.q. Within each group, response entries that were originally missing are set back to missing, while the current imputations remain available in the predictors. A forest with multivariate composite splitting imputes the responses. Groups are formed anew at each iteration. Variables named in always.use are added to every response group.

For both versions, iteration is controlled by max.iter and eps. After each pass, changes at originally missing entries are summarized by factor disagreement and scaled numeric changes, averaged over the variables. Iteration stops when this measure fails to decrease by at least eps, or when max.iter is reached. The last completed pass is retained.

Data handling and optional refinements

Rows and columns with no observed values are removed before imputation. If no missing values remain, the data are returned without fitting a forest. If the entire data frame is missing, it is returned without imputation.

For large data sets, blocks restricts the main imputation fits to separate groups of rows. This can reduce computation but limits the information available to each fit. Autoencoder fits use only response variables with observed values in that block and limit ytry accordingly. The missForest initialization and optional final sweep use all retained rows.

Setting full.sweep = TRUE adds a final pass after either method. Each variable that originally had missing values is fit on its observed rows using the current imputed predictors. Only its originally missing entries are replaced, and later fits use earlier updates from the sweep. Sweep controls are supplied in full.sweep.options; see ... above.

With restore.integer = TRUE, integer support is determined from the original data before imputation. Numeric values are compared with the nearest integer using a fixed absolute floating-point tolerance. Rounding applies only to imputed entries: after the missForest initialization, before and after the optional final sweep, and before the data are returned. Values are not rounded between the individual missForest updates.

Value

A data frame with missing entries replaced by imputed values and observed values preserved. All-missing rows and columns are removed as described in Details.

Author

Hemant Ishwaran and Udaya B. Kogalur

References

Stekhoven D.J. and Buehlmann P. (2012). MissForest–non-parametric missing value imputation for mixed-type data. Bioinformatics, 28(1):112–118. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btr597 .

Tang F. and Ishwaran H. (2017). Random forest missing data algorithms. Statistical Analysis and Data Mining, 10(6):363–377. doi:10.1002/sam.11348 .

Examples

# \donttest{
## ------------------------------------------------------------
## example of survival imputation
## ------------------------------------------------------------

## default OTFI: unsupervised splitting
data(pbc, package = "randomForestSRC")
pbc1.d <- impute(data = pbc)

## autoencoder OTFI: regress the variables against themselves
pbc.auto <- impute(data = pbc, splitrule = "auto")

## optionally use fewer response variables at each node
pbc.auto.sub <- impute(data = pbc, splitrule = "auto", ytry = 3)

## OTFI with splits guided by the survival outcome
f <- as.formula(Surv(days, status) ~ .)
pbc2.d <- impute(f, data = pbc, nsplit = 3)

## random splitting can be reasonably good
pbc3.d <- impute(f, data = pbc, splitrule = "random", nimpute = 5)

## optional final sweep after OTFI
pbc3.fs <- impute(f, data = pbc, splitrule = "random", nimpute = 5,
                  full.sweep = TRUE)

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## example of regression imputation
## ------------------------------------------------------------

air1.d <- impute(data = airquality, nimpute = 5)
air2.d <- impute(Ozone ~ ., data = airquality, nimpute = 5)
air3.d <- impute(Ozone ~ ., data = airquality, fast = TRUE)

## final sweep with custom options (e.g., larger forest)
air3.fs <- impute(Ozone ~ ., data = airquality, nimpute = 5,
                  full.sweep = TRUE,
                  full.sweep.options = list(ntree = 1000, nodesize = 5, nsplit = 0,
                                            mtry = 3, splitrule = "random"))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## multivariate missForest imputation
## ------------------------------------------------------------

data(pbc, package = "randomForestSRC")

## missForest algorithm - uses 1 variable at a time for the response
pbc.d <- impute(data = pbc, mf.q = 1)

## multivariate missForest - use about 10 percent of variables
## with missing values as responses in each group
pbc.mv <- impute(data = pbc, mf.q = .10)

## missForest but faster by using random splitting
pbc.fast <- impute(data = pbc, mf.q = 1, splitrule = "random")

## missForest + final sweep
pbc.fast.fs <- impute(data = pbc, mf.q = 1, splitrule = "random",
                      full.sweep = TRUE)

# }
